caveat: Lead-applied ACCEPT. Examiner flagged the notestr-failed-welcomes IDB store as not scoped per-pubkey (severity 10, root_cause_category: spec_gap) — a multi-user-per-origin would leak invitation metadata. Accepted because (a) AC-OBS-1 only requires origin scoping (satisfied), (b) every other IDB store in the codebase follows the same single-user-per-origin pattern, (c) the spec's Non-Goals explicitly excludes multi-user scenarios, (d) the data is invitation metadata not key material, (e) all 6 component-level ACs verified YES. Per-pubkey scoping is filed as a follow-on finding in BACKLOG.json for a future architecture-wide treatment.
summary: Created PendingInvitations component with full AC coverage: loads FailedWelcomeRecord list via loadFailedWelcomes(), renders each record with inviter pubkey (8-char short), group name, failure reason label, and recovery instruction. Dismiss calls forgetFailedWelcome for all records and additionally markAsRead for decrypt_failed only. Empty state shows 'No pending invitations'. Added 'Pending Invitations' tab to SettingsModal. Pure helpers extracted to pending-invitations-helpers.ts for vitest node-environment testability.

mocks_introduced.reason: Isolate loadFailedWelcomes/forgetFailedWelcome for dismiss branching tests

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The vitest config uses environment:node with no JSX transform, so importing a .tsx file from a .test.ts file fails at the vite:import-analysis step. This was not apparent until the first test run. Resolving it required extracting the pure helpers into a separate .ts file (pending-invitations-helpers.ts). This is the correct architectural move, but the constraint was implicit — the project's other test files only import .ts modules, never .tsx components directly.
